components.name: Avatar
components.description: A circular container that represents a person or entity — showing their image when available and falling back to initials otherwise. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg), can carry an optional online status dot, and binds its surface, text, and circular shape to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Represent a person or entity with an image or their initials
Show presence with the optional online status dot
whenNotToUse: Displaying a decorative or brand image — use a plain image
As a button — wrap it in a Button or link if it must be interactive

size.sm: 32px — dense lists, comments, and inline mentions.
size.md: 40px — default, for most rows and headers.
size.lg: 48px — profile headers and other prominent placements.

states.default: Shows the image when a source is provided.
states.fallback: No image — shows the initials on the muted surface instead.
states.status: Optional online dot anchored to the bottom-right corner.

dos: Provide meaningful alt text when showing a photo
Give a sensible initials fallback for when the image is missing
Keep initials to one or two characters
donts: Don't rely on the status dot alone to convey presence — pair with text where it matters
Don't stretch non-square images — the image is cropped to a circle
Don't use an avatar as the only label for a person in dense UI without a name nearby

keyboard: Not interactive on its own; if made actionable, wrap in a focusable control
notes: A photo needs descriptive alt text; initials are read as text
The status dot is decorative (aria-hidden) — surface presence in text where it matters
Sufficient contrast between initials and the muted background is token-guaranteed

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Labels a status, count, or category.
components.description: A small pill-shaped label for short status, counts, or categories. It comes in four tones (default / secondary / destructive / outline), takes an optional leading icon, and binds its color, spacing, and full-radius shape to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Call out a status, state, or category — "Active", "Beta", "3 new"
Attach a short, at-a-glance label to another element
whenNotToUse: Triggering an action — use a Button
A removable or selectable token in an input — use a Chip

variant.default: Solid brand fill — highest emphasis, for the primary status.
variant.destructive: Solid danger fill — errors, blocked, or critical states.
variant.outline: Bordered with a transparent fill — the quietest tone.

states.default: Static label — a Badge is presentational and has no interactive states.

dos: Keep the text to a word or two
Bind the color to a semantic tone that matches the meaning
Pair color with text or an icon so the meaning survives without color
donts: Don't rely on color alone to convey status
Don't put an interactive control inside a badge — use a Button or Chip
Don't write full sentences — a badge is a label, not a message

keyboard: Not interactive and not focusable
notes: Renders as inline text, so the label is read in reading order
Convey status with text or an icon, not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
A leading icon is decorative (aria-hidden) — the text carries the meaning

components.name: Button
components.description: A clickable control that starts an action: saving a form, confirming a choice, opening a dialog. Its emphasis levels signal how important an action is, so the choice of variant is the main decision when you use it.
whenToUse: The user needs to make something happen on the current page, like saving, confirming, or opening a dialog.
A view needs one obvious primary action.
whenNotToUse: The control takes the user to another page or URL. Use a Link; the link variant only looks like a link and still triggers an action.

variant.default: The one main action in a view.
variant.secondary: A supporting action that sits beside the main one.
variant.destructive: An action that deletes something or cannot be undone.
variant.outline: A quieter action that still needs a visible edge.
variant.ghost: The quietest action, for toolbars and dense layouts.
variant.link: An action that reads as inline text.

size.md: The default size for most uses.
size.lg: For hero moments that need extra presence.

states.default: At rest and ready to be clicked.
states.hover: The pointer is over the button and it lightens to invite a click.
states.focus: The button has keyboard focus and shows a focus ring.
states.disabled: Can't be clicked or tabbed to.
states.loading: The action is running; a spinner replaces the leading icon until it finishes.

dos: Lead the label with a verb.
Keep one primary button per view.
Keep labels to about three words.
donts: Don't use a button to navigate. Use a Link.
Don't stack two primary buttons in one view.
Don't disable a button without telling the user why.

keyboard: Enter activates the button.
Space activates the button.
notes: An icon-only button needs an aria-label so screen readers can announce it.
A disabled or loading button can't take keyboard focus. Say why it is unavailable somewhere a screen reader will reach.

components.name: Card
components.summary: Groups related content and actions about a single subject.
components.description: A container that gathers everything about one subject — a person, a product, a project — so it reads as a single unit in a list or a grid. Give each card one clear main action; a card with several competing actions stops being one unit.
whenToUse: Several pieces of information belong to one subject and should be scanned together.
The page shows a list or grid of comparable items.
whenNotToUse: You need page-level layout structure. Use the page's own layout instead.
The content is a plain run of text with nothing to group. Leave it ungrouped.

variant.default: The everyday choice, separated from the page by a thin edge.
variant.elevated: Lifts off the page, for a card that sits above other content or needs emphasis.

dos: Make the main action obvious.
Keep one main call-to-action per card.
donts: Don't nest cards more than one level deep.
Don't make the card and a button inside it separately clickable.

notes: A card is just a container with no meaning of its own. Add a role and a name only when it is a landmark region or is itself clickable.
If the whole card is clickable, give it an accessible name and make it reachable by keyboard.
Don't let the lift be the only thing carrying meaning; anyone who can't see it needs the same information in words.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: A control for an independent on/off choice, rendered as a button with role="checkbox". It supports checked, unchecked, and indeterminate (a partial-selection dash) states across the full interaction set — default, hover, focus, active, and disabled — and binds its fill, border, radius, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Offer an independent on/off choice, like accepting terms
Select any number of options from a list (zero, one, or many)
Represent a parent's partial selection with the indeterminate state
whenNotToUse: Choosing exactly one option from a set — use a Radio group
A single setting that applies immediately with no Save — use a Switch

checked.false: Unchecked — empty box with a neutral border.
checked.true: Checked — brand fill with a check glyph.
checked.indeterminate: Partial — brand fill with a dash, for a mixed parent state.

states.hover: Pointer over the box — border strengthens when unchecked.
states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Give every checkbox a visible, clickable label
Use the indeterminate state only for a parent summarizing mixed children
Group related checkboxes under a clear group label
donts: Don't use a checkbox for a one-of-many choice — that's a Radio group
Don't use it for a setting that takes effect instantly — prefer a Switch
Don't leave the box unlabeled or rely on placement alone for meaning

keyboard: Space toggles the checkbox
Tab moves focus to and from the control
notes: State is exposed via aria-checked, with "mixed" for indeterminate
Disabled checkboxes are dimmed and not interactive
The visible label should be programmatically associated with the control

components.name: Input
components.summary: Collects a single line of free-form text.
components.description: A single-line field for text the user types themselves, like a name, an email address, or a search query. It always needs a visible label, and the error state is what most changes how you use it: reserve room for the message so the layout doesn't jump.
whenToUse: The answer is short, open-ended text that you can't offer as a list of choices.
The user is searching or filtering and needs to type freely.
whenNotToUse: The answer comes from a fixed set of options. Use Select for many choices or Radio for a few.
The answer runs to several lines, like a comment or a description. Use Textarea.

size.md: The default size for most forms.

states.default: At rest and ready to accept typing.
states.focus: The field has keyboard focus and shows a focus ring.
states.error: What the user typed didn't pass validation, and the message says why.
states.disabled: Can't be typed in or tabbed to.

dos: Pair every field with a visible label.
Put format hints in helper text.
Reserve space for the error message.
donts: Don't use the placeholder as the only label. Add a real label.
Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur.

keyboard: Standard text-editing keys apply.
Tab moves focus to and from the field.
notes: Give every field a label element that points at it. A placeholder disappears as soon as the user types, so it can't do this job.
In the error state, set aria-invalid and link the message with aria-describedby so screen readers announce it.
Mark a decorative leading icon aria-hidden so it isn't announced.

components.name: Radio
components.summary: Selects one option from a set.
components.description: A control for choosing exactly one option from a set, rendered as a button with role="radio" and coordinated by a RadioGroup wrapper that holds the selected value. Each radio shows selected or unselected across the full interaction set — default, hover, focus, active, and disabled — and binds its border, brand inner dot, circular shape, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Choose exactly one option from a small, visible set of choices
Present mutually exclusive options where seeing them all matters
whenNotToUse: Selecting more than one option — use Checkboxes
Choosing from a long list — use a Select to save space

selected.false: Unselected — empty circle with a neutral border.
selected.true: Selected — brand ring with a filled brand inner dot.

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Wrap radios in a RadioGroup with a clear group label
Give each radio a visible, clickable label
Preselect a sensible default when one clearly applies
donts: Don't use a radio group to allow multiple selections — use Checkboxes
Don't offer a single lone radio — that choice can't be deselected; use a Checkbox
Don't split one logical choice across multiple groups

keyboard: Arrow keys move selection between radios in the group
Tab moves focus into and out of the group as a whole
notes: The group carries role="radiogroup"; each option exposes aria-checked
Only the selected radio (or the first, if none) is in the tab order
Disabled radios are dimmed and skipped

components.name: Select
components.summary: Chooses one option from a dropdown list.
components.description: An accessible trigger for choosing one option from a list, wrapping a native select so it inherits the platform's open/close and keyboard behavior. A non-interactive chevron sits on the trailing edge. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg) with default, focus, error, and disabled states, and binds its background, border, radius, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Choose a single option from a moderate-to-long list
Save vertical space when a Radio group would be too many options
whenNotToUse: A short set of a few options that benefit from being visible — use Radios
Selecting more than one value — use a multi-select or checkboxes

error.false: Default — neutral border and focus ring.
error.true: Error — destructive border and ring to flag an invalid choice.

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Always pair with a visible label
Order options predictably (alphabetical, or by frequency)
Provide a clear default or an unselected placeholder option
donts: Don't use a Select for only two or three visible options — use Radios
Don't hide critical actions inside a Select — it's for choosing values
Don't rely on the placeholder as the field's only label

keyboard: Enter or Space / Arrow keys open and move through options
Typing jumps to matching options; Tab moves focus to and from the field
notes: Built on a native <select>, so platform semantics and behavior come for free
The chevron is decorative (aria-hidden) — the native control carries behavior
The error state sets aria-invalid and links the message via aria-describedby

components.name: Select Menu
components.summary: The dropdown surface that holds selectable options.
components.description: The popover surface opened from a Select trigger — a bordered, elevated panel with role="listbox" that holds a list of Select Menu Items passed as its content. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg) and binds its surface, border, radius, and elevation to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Present the list of options opened from a Select trigger
Group a set of Select Menu Items into one scrollable, elevated surface
whenNotToUse: A menu of actions or commands — use a Menu, not a listbox
Free-form text entry — use an Input or Textarea

size.sm: Compact — pairs with a small Select trigger.
size.lg: Roomier — pairs with a large Select trigger.

states.default: Open surface holding its items; visibility is controlled by the Select.

dos: Fill it with Select Menu Items and keep them consistently sized
Match the menu size to the Select trigger that opens it
Let long lists scroll rather than overflowing the surface
donts: Don't mix unrelated actions into an option listbox
Don't nest another menu surface inside a single option
Don't hardcode its elevation or radius — they come from tokens

keyboard: Arrow keys move through options; Enter selects
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger
notes: Carries role="listbox"; its children are role="option"
Selection and active option are exposed via aria-selected and focus
Opened and closed from the Select trigger, which owns the expanded state

components.name: Select Menu Item
components.summary: One selectable row inside a Select Menu.
components.description: A single selectable option within a Select Menu, rendered with role="option". Its label is passed as content and a trailing check appears when it is the current selection. It covers the full interaction set — default, hover, focused (keyboard navigation), selected, and disabled — and binds its text, surfaces, and the selected check to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Represent one choosable option inside a Select Menu listbox
Mark the currently selected value with the trailing check
whenNotToUse: A clickable action or command — use a Menu item, not an option
Standalone outside a Select Menu — items only make sense within the listbox

selected.false: Not the current value — no trailing check.
selected.true: Current value — subtle fill and a trailing brand check.

states.hover: Pointer over the row — subtle background.
states.focused: Keyboard navigation highlight — muted background with a focus ring.
states.selected: The current value — subtle fill and trailing check.

dos: Keep option labels short and scannable
Let the trailing check be the single, consistent selected indicator
Keep items visually uniform within one menu
donts: Don't put multiple interactive controls inside one option row
Don't convey selection by color alone — the check carries it too
Don't use an option row for an action — that belongs in a Menu

keyboard: Reachable via the parent listbox's arrow-key navigation
Enter selects the focused option
notes: Carries role="option" with aria-selected reflecting the current value
Disabled options set aria-disabled and leave the tab order
Selection is shown with a check, not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)

components.name: Spinner
components.description: A continuously spinning loader that signals an indeterminate wait — an action in progress or a region still loading. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg), takes its color from the foreground token, and exposes an accessible "Loading" status to assistive technology.
whenToUse: Signal that an action is in progress — a button submitting, a panel fetching
Fill a region that is still loading when you can't show real content yet
whenNotToUse: Showing how far along a known task is — use a determinate progress bar
Long or content-heavy loads where a skeleton better previews the layout

size.sm: 16px — inline with text or inside a small control like a button.
size.md: 24px — default, for standalone or region-level loading.
size.lg: 32px — prominent, for full-panel or page-level waits.

states.default: Continuously animating (spinning) — the spinner has no resting or interactive states.

dos: Give the spinner an accessible label so screen readers announce the wait
Match the size to its context — small inside controls, larger for regions
Pair a longer wait with a short message so users know what's happening
donts: Don't use a spinner for progress you can actually measure
Don't leave a spinner running with no resolution or timeout
Don't rely on the spin alone — expose a text status for assistive tech

keyboard: Not interactive and not focusable — it conveys status only
notes: Wrapper carries role="status" with an aria-label (defaults to "Loading")
The spinning glyph is aria-hidden so only the status text is announced
role="status" announces politely without stealing focus

components.name: Switch
components.summary: Toggles a single setting on or off.
components.description: A toggle for a single on/off setting that takes effect immediately, rendered as a button with role="switch". The track fills with the brand color when on and a muted color when off, with an adaptive thumb whose visible edge is carried by a strong border. It covers off, on, and disabled states and binds every color and the focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Turn a single setting on or off with an immediate effect
Offer a binary preference that doesn't need a separate Save
whenNotToUse: A choice that only applies after submitting a form — use a Checkbox
Choosing one of several options — use a Radio group

checked.false: Off — muted track, thumb to the left.
checked.true: On — brand track, thumb slid to the right.

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Use a clear label that reads as an on/off state
Apply the change immediately when toggled
Keep the label stable — don't relabel the switch as it flips
donts: Don't require a separate Save for a switch — that's a Checkbox pattern
Don't use a switch for non-binary choices
Don't rely on the thumb position alone — pair with a visible label

keyboard: Space toggles the switch
Tab moves focus to and from the control
notes: On/off is exposed via aria-checked
The thumb keeps a >=3:1 edge against the track via a strong border for low-vision users
Disabled switches are dimmed and not interactive

components.name: Textarea
components.description: The multi-line sibling of Input: a styled native textarea that fills its container, grows vertically as needed, and shares Input's token-driven border, background, and focus ring. It covers default, focus, error, and disabled states and can flag invalid input with a destructive border and ring.
whenToUse: Collect longer, multi-line free-form text — comments, descriptions, notes
Give users room to write more than a single line comfortably
whenNotToUse: A single line of text — use an Input
Choosing from a fixed set of options — use a Select or Radio group

error.false: Default — neutral border and focus ring.
error.true: Error — destructive border and ring to flag invalid input.

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Always pair with a visible label
Show format or length hints as helper text
Reserve space for error text to avoid layout shift
donts: Don't use placeholder text as the only label
Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur
Don't fix the height so short that users can't see what they wrote

keyboard: Standard text editing and caret navigation
Tab moves focus to and from the field
notes: Associate a visible <label> with the field programmatically
The error state sets aria-invalid and links the message via aria-describedby
Users can resize vertically; don't disable resize without reason

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: Shows a brief hint on hover or focus.
components.description: A lightweight text hint that reveals on hover or keyboard focus of its trigger. It can be placed on any of four sides (top / right / bottom / left) with an arrow pointing back to the trigger, and binds its surface, text, radius, and elevation to the system's semantic tokens. Because it reveals on focus, the trigger must itself be focusable.
whenToUse: Add a short, supplementary hint to a control — what an icon button does
Clarify a label or value without taking up permanent space
whenNotToUse: Essential information a user must not miss — put it inline
Rich or interactive content — use a Popover instead

side.top: Bubble above the trigger — the default.
side.right: Bubble to the right of the trigger.
side.left: Bubble to the left of the trigger.

states.visible: Revealed on hover or focus of the trigger.

dos: Keep the text short — a phrase, not a paragraph
Attach the tooltip to a focusable trigger so keyboard users get it too
Use it for supplementary hints, not essential instructions
donts: Don't hide essential information only inside a tooltip
Don't put links, buttons, or form fields inside — use a Popover
Don't attach a tooltip to a non-focusable element — keyboard users can't reach it

keyboard: Reveals on focus of the trigger and hides on blur
Escape should dismiss it while the trigger stays focused
notes: The bubble carries role="tooltip"; the trigger must be focusable
Reveals on both hover and focus so it isn't pointer-only
Keep the hint supplementary — don't make it the only source of critical info
